newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican fluorspar mines seen reactivated this year.
newsitem.headline: Mexican fluorspar mines seen reactivated this year.

text.p: Flourspar mining will see a new lease of life in the central state of Guanajuato in the first quarter of 1997 because mining companies plan to reactivate mines there, an official said.

Industrias Luismin unit Minas de San Luis and Industrial Minera Mexico, the mining arm of Grupo Mexico, are heading a group of companies aiming to resume flourspar mining, said the official, who requested anonimity.
Luismin is the mining arm of Sanluis Corporacion.

Most of the mine reactivation will be done in the north of the state in the areas of El Realito and Rio Colorado, with the companies also contemplating a production plant in the area around the town of Los Alamos de Martinez.
Mining in the area was suspended in 1991 after a fall of international flourspar prices. It was the fourth largest production area in the country, with an output of more than 135,000 tonnes.
Fluorspar is a mineral used in the production of hydrochloric acid, aluminium and steel.

Jesus Franco Ibarra, director of mining development for the Guanajuato state, confirmed at least eight companies were joining forces to reactivate output. "They have agreed to set up an asociation of fluorspar producers," he said.
Franco said authorities plan to meet with the mining companies on Feb 10 in the town of San Luis de la Paz to discuss plans and go over financing options.
Mexico's biggest fluorspar miner is Grupo Industrial Camesa. It produced 420,000 tonnes in 1996 against 370,000 tonnes in 1995.
